title: Split Gibbs Discrete Diffusion Posterior Sampling

problem.statement: Posterior sampling p(x|y) in DISCRETE-state spaces using a pretrained discrete diffusion model as a plug-and-play prior. Covers inverse problems (y = G(x)+n) and reward-guided generation (p(y|x) ~ exp(beta*r(x))). Continuous DPS methods do not transfer because log p(y|x) has no gradient on a finite support.
problem.contribution: SGDD: a plug-and-play posterior sampler built on the SPLIT GIBBS principle. Introduce an auxiliary variable z and a potential D(x,z;eta) (Hamming-distance based, Eq 10) that relaxes the problem into an augmented distribution pi(x,z;eta) (Eq 7). Alternate: (1) LIKELIHOOD step z~pi(x=x_k,z;eta) via Metropolis-Hastings (Eq 13), (2) PRIOR step x~pi(x,z=z_k;eta) which is equivalent to a partial discrete-diffusion denoising from sigma_t=eta, x_t=z_k (Eq 11-12). Both marginals provably converge to p(x|y) as eta->0. Theorem 1 gives an O(1/K) Fisher-divergence convergence bound accounting for score + discretization error.

core_algorithm.name: Algorithm 1 — SplitGibbsDiscreteDiffusion (SGDD)
loop: likelihood step (Eq 13): z_k ~ pi(x=x_k, z; eta_k)  via Metropolis-Hastings, T steps
prior step (Eq 11): x_{k+1} ~ pi(x, z=z_k; eta_k)   via H-step Euler discrete-diffusion denoise from eta_k
core_algorithm.potential: D(x,z;eta) = d(x,z) * log[ (1 + (N-1)e^{-eta}) / ((N-1)(1-e^{-eta})) ], d = Hamming distance (Eq 10). D->inf as eta->0 unless d(x,z)=0, which forces both marginals to the posterior.
core_algorithm.prior_step_identity: pi(x,z=z_k;eta) ~ p0(x) * (beta~/(1-beta~))^{d(z_k,x)} with beta~ = (N-1)/N (1-e^{-eta}). This equals unconditional p(x0|xt) denoising when beta~ = beta_t, i.e. eta = sigma_t. So the prior step IS a partial reverse discrete-diffusion sampler started at noise level eta from state z_k.
core_algorithm.likelihood_step: z_k ~ exp(-f(z;y) - d(x,z)*log[...]) with f(z;y) = -log p(y|z). Unnormalized density is accessible -> sample by Metropolis-Hastings (no likelihood gradient needed). This is the key enabler for discrete data.
core_algorithm.convergence: Theorem 1: average relative Fisher information between non-stationary mu_t and stationary pi_t over K prior steps <= 2KL(pi0||mu0)/(K t*) + 4 M eps / c + 2 M L t* / (c H). O(1/K) convergence + bounded score/discretization error.

prior_model.type: SEDD (Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion, Lou et al. [29]) with UNIFORM transition kernel Qfw = (1/N) 11^T - I
prior_model.size: SEDD-small, ~90M params, used for ALL real-data experiments
prior_model.note: For the synthetic benchmark the prior is a CLOSED-FORM concrete score (discretized Gaussian) — NO trained weights needed. This is what makes the algorithm CPU-verifiable end-to-end against a known posterior.

method.noise_schedule: Geometric annealing eta_k = eta_min^{k/K} * eta_max^{1-k/K}, eta_min=1e-4, eta_max=20 (Sec C.3). Anneals large->0 to accelerate mixing (Sec B.1).

experiments.name: Synthetic (controlled posterior)
experiments.setup: Prior = discretized Gaussian N(0, sigma^2 I_D) on a D-dim grid, vocab N=50. Forward model G(x)=||f(x)||_1. TRUE posterior is computable, so accuracy is measurable exactly.

experiments.name: Guided DNA enhancers (reward guidance)
experiments.setup: SEDD trained on Gosai et al. ~700k MPRA DNA seqs; reward oracle r(.) predicts HepG2 activity; p(y|x) ~ exp(beta r(x)). 640 samples.
experiments.gated_on: SEDD-90M DNA weights + two reward oracles + ATAC classifier

algorithm.why: Algorithm 1 + Eq 7-13 are fully specified in-text; potential D (Eq 10), prior-step identity (Eq 11-12), MH likelihood step (Eq 13), and geometric schedule (Sec C.3) all given explicitly. Public reference code exists.

synthetic_benchmark.why: Discretized-Gaussian prior + G(x)=||f(x)||_1; true posterior computable. Exact hparams in Table 7 (K=10, T=10, H=20, N=50). Fully CPU-reproducible.

real_data_metrics.why: DNA/MNIST/music all need the trained SEDD-90M priors + task-specific oracles/classifiers. Numbers taken verbatim from Tables 3-5; reproduction of these is weight-gated.
